title: Algorithmic Attention and Content Creation on Social Media Platforms
abstract: arXiv:2609.15573v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: We study revenue-maximizing attention allocation on an ad-funded social media platform governed by recommendation algorithms. Attention is costly and can be monetized through advertising or allocated to increase creators' exposure, creating a trade-off between monetization and production incentives. In a two-sided model with heterogeneous viewers and creators under private information, the optimal recommendation mix includes content that is ex post suboptimal for some viewers to leverage network externalities. These distortions are targeted: low-ability creators are excluded, while high-ability creators are subsidized through exposure or monetary payments. Two-sided complementarities reshape content variety and quality, with implications for personalization regulation and advertising markets.

translated_title: 社交媒体平台上的算法注意力与内容创作
translated_abstract: 我们研究了由推荐算法主导的广告资助型社交媒体平台上收益最大化的注意力分配问题。注意力是有成本的，既可以通过广告变现，也可以分配给创作者以增加其曝光度，从而在变现与创作激励之间形成权衡。在一个包含私有信息下异质性观众和创作者的双边模型中，最优推荐组合会包含对部分观众事后次优的内容，以利用网络外部性。这些扭曲具有针对性：低能力创作者被排除在外，而高能力创作者则通过曝光或货币支付获得补贴。双边互补性重塑了内容的多样性和质量，对个性化监管和广告市场具有重要意义。
tldr: 本文研究了广告资助的社交媒体平台上推荐算法如何最优分配用户注意力，发现平台在变现与创作者激励之间权衡时，会策略性地推荐事后次优内容、排除低能力创作者并补贴高能力创作者，以利用网络外部性。
en_tdlr: This paper studies how recommendation algorithms optimally allocate user attention on ad-funded social media platforms, showing that platforms strategically recommend ex post suboptimal content, exclude low-ability creators, and subsidize high-ability creators to leverage network externalities when balancing monetization against production incentives.
